subject: Re: Rate limits & overage pricing — follow-up
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — rate limits & pricing follow-up

Thanks again for the call today, Jordan — good to meet you and the Acme team. Quick recap and a couple of follow-ups so we can align on pricing/quotas: 

Summary from my side:
- Desired integration: user-facing product features (chat + summarization) with ~2M tokens/day baseline, with periodic spikes tied to marketing campaigns.
- Peak expectation: you mentioned spikes up to ~8–12M tokens/day for 1–2 days when campaigns run.
- Target unit economics: you asked for target $/1M tokens — mentioned a rough internal target of $20–$30/1M but wanted Redwood to propose options.

Asks for you (to confirm):
1) Can you confirm typical baseline vs peak (average daily tokens, and typical spike duration)?
2) Are spikes predictable (scheduled campaigns) or unpredictable/burst-driven?
3) Any hard latency SLOs for user-facing responses (p95, acceptable tail latency)?

On our side I asked SE to outline rate limit mechanics, quota increase process, and overage pricing. I’ve attached an initial SOW draft and will share a short rate-limits summary from our SE team once they confirm.

Next steps: if you confirm the token volumes and target price range, we’ll propose two commercial options (committed baseline with discounted unit price + burst/overage terms; and on-demand pricing for variable usage). Can we aim to finalize preferred model by end of week? Happy to hop on a quick follow to walk numbers.

Thanks,
Camila
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.ai

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call recap — rate limits & pricing follow-up

Thanks Camila — that matches what we discussed. A few clarifications: 

- Baseline: roughly 1.8–2.2M tokens/day on weekdays; weekends drop to ~600–800k.
- Spikes: typically campaign-driven and fairly predictable; we schedule campaigns ~4–6 times per quarter. Spikes historically hit 8–12M tokens/day for 24–48 hours. Occasionally we see an unplanned viral event (rare) that can sustain high volume for 3–4 days.
- Latency: user-facing calls need p95 < 500ms token latency (we care about overall response time; can discuss exact p95 metric).
- Pricing: our procurement team is targeting around $25/1M tokens for committed volume; for uncommitted burst/overage they can accept a premium but would like to understand how high that premium is (e.g., 1.5x, 2x, fixed $/1M).

Procurement is cc’d for visibility — they’ll want the formal SOW and any contract language around quota increases and overage billing.

—Jordan
Head of Product, Acme Corp
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>

Aditya / Marissa — forwarding Jordan’s clarification. Key asks: confirm we can support baseline ~2M/day with burst to 10–12M/day for 24–48h, p95 latency target ~500ms, and provide a clear overage pricing approach they can take to procurement. 

Questions for SE:
- What default per-customer rate limit (tokens/sec or tokens/min) would we apply for a customer on a committed plan?
- Can we allow short-term quota increases without a new contract (self-serve request or manual approval)? Lead time?
- What overage pricing mechanics do we recommend (flat multiplier vs tiered $/1M)? Any examples from similar deals?

I’ve attached the SOW draft I sent to Jordan — if we’re aligned on numbers I’ll send a revised SOW with the pricing table.

Thanks,
Camila
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Post-call recap — rate limits & pricing follow-up

Thanks for the context — data below based on current offering and what we can reasonably support for Acme’s profile. I’ve also attached a short rate-limits summary (rate-limits-summary.csv) for internal reference.

Baseline & bursting
- Committed baseline: 2M tokens/day is straightforward — recommend committing at the monthly level (multiply daily baseline by 30) to get a stable unit price.
- Burst behavior: we support bursts up to ~5x baseline for short periods (24–48 hrs) if pre-warmed and signed off by infra ops. For Acme that maps to ~10M/day bursts. Unpredictable multi-day viral events (3–4 days) are treated case-by-case and may require capacity pre-commit or temporary throttling.

Rate limits
- Default quota: 120,000 tokens/minute (2,000 tokens/sec) for committed customers.
- Can increase to 300,000 tokens/minute (5,000 tokens/sec) with quota request and validation (typically 48–72h lead time if no infra changes).
- For immediate short bursts we can provision higher soft-limits for 24–48h if requested 24h in advance and approved by infra (subject to capacity).

Overage & pricing options
Option A — Committed baseline + burst/overage multiplier (recommended for predictable customers):
- Baseline unit price: $25/1M tokens (matches their target).
- Overage/burst multiplier: 1.8x baseline for on-demand bursts beyond committed quota (i.e., $45/1M). Overage billed monthly.

Option B — Tiered overage (smoother for procurement):
- Baseline (committed): $25/1M.
- Overage 0–2x baseline/month: $40/1M.
- Overage >2x baseline/month: $55/1M.

Option C — On-demand (no commitment): $60/1M across the board (simpler but higher unit cost).

Notes & recommendations:
- For Acme I recommend Option A with a formal committed baseline (2M/day => ~60M/month) at $25/1M and 1.8x burst multiplier. That gives them a predictable baseline and a clear cap on short-term burst cost.
- We should include a documented quota increase process in the SOW (self-serve request + manual approval path + 48–72h typical turnaround).
- If procurement wants a hard cap on spend for bursts, we can add a pre-approval gating mechanism.

Next steps:
- I’ll prepare a one-page pricing table you can send to Jordan + procurement.
- If they like Option A, we draft SOW with baseline commitment, burst multiplier, and quota-increase appendix.

—Aditya
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Proposal: committed baseline + burst terms (summary)

Jordan — thanks for the quick answers. Based on Aditya’s recommendations, here’s a concise proposal for procurement to review: 

Commercial summary (recommended):
- Committed baseline: 60M tokens/month (approx. 2M/day) at $25/1M tokens.
- Burst/overage: 1.8x multiplier on baseline for short on-demand bursts (billed monthly) => $45/1M. Bursts are supported up to ~5x baseline for 24–48h with 24h notice; longer uncontrolled multi-day spikes handled case-by-case.
- Default rate limit: 120k tokens/minute. Quota increases to 300k tokens/minute available with 48–72h validation; immediate 24–48h soft-limit increases possible with 24h notice subject to infra approval.
- Optional: hard spend cap for bursts can be added to the SOW if procurement wants guaranteed spend ceiling.

Attachments: I’ve attached a revised SOW draft that includes the pricing table and a short appendix describing quota-increase workflows. If this looks right, approve and we’ll circulate a final SOW and order form.

Proposed next step: 30-minute procurement + product call tomorrow to walk SOW and get sign-off. Does 10am PT work for you?

Thanks — happy to adjust numbers if procurement has contraints.

Camila
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

—Jordan
